subject: CrowdWorks dedicated footprint inquiry and migration plan
messages:
From: Paul Moreno <paul@crowdworks.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity question — CrowdWorks API migration

Hi Vivek,

We're moving our primary NLU stack to a dedicated endpoint and evaluating Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput. High level: we currently run a mix of chat-style assistant calls and short classification requests. I attached a sample of 48 hours of traffic (cw_workload_samples.csv).

Key asks:
- Rough GPU footprint to support peak concurrency of ~180 active sessions (concurrency defined as in-flight generation requests).
- How you estimate steady vs burst capacity and what you recommend for a conservative canary.
- Any constraints on prompt/response sizes we should be aware of when picking a model variant.

We target p95 generation latency <600ms for the chat path and are happy to trade a small amount of throughput for latency guarantees. Happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Thanks,
Paul Moreno
Head of Platform
CrowdWorks Inc

--- attachment: cw_workload_samples.csv (CSV, 12KB)

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Paul Moreno <paul@crowdworks.ai>, procurement@crowdworks.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — CrowdWorks API migration

Paul — thanks for the sample. Quick clarifying questions before we do a sizing pass:

1) Traffic shape: is the 48h capture representative of your normal week (no special promo or incident)?
2) Prompt/response tokens: can you provide typical prompt tokens and typical model tokens per request for the two paths (chat assistant vs classification)? If you don’t have exact counts, ballpark averages are fine.
3) SLA targets: you mentioned p95 <600ms for chat — do you have the same constraint for classification requests?
4) Canary constraints: what fraction of production traffic do you want routed to Dedicated during canary (e.g., 5%, 25%)?

I’ll loop in Marissa (workload modeling) and Ben (capacity economics) and we’ll produce a first-pass estimate and a recommended canary plan.

Best,
Vivek
Director, Pre-Sales
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-04T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity question — data and first-pass notes

Quick pass on the CSV Paul sent. High-level extracts and assumptions:

- Capture looks clean and not a promotional spike — timestamp distribution shows steady diurnal behavior with two daily peaks.
- Peak observed RPS (summed across endpoints) = 95 rps; 99th-percentile short window bursts reach ~210 rps for <30s windows.
- Session concurrency: their definition (in-flight generation requests) aligns with our modeling; observed peak concurrent in-flight requests in sample ~165.
- Token assumptions (from their example rows): median prompt ~48 tokens; median generated tokens ~330 for chat path. Classification path median prompt 22 tokens and response 8 tokens.

Initial sizing heuristics:
- Latency target p95 <600ms with median gen ~330 tokens suggests we likely need a lower-quantized model variant and moderate batching headroom.
- For cost/latency balance, recommend planning for a dedicated pool sized for sustainable 120 rps (to cover steady high) with headroom for bursts up to 220 rps using autoscaling + short-lived burst capacity.
- Translate to GPUs: for redwood-7b-v2-like runtime, rough token throughput per A100-80GB equiv node (conservative) ~13k tokens/sec sustained; H100 throughput ~1.6x that.

I’ll run concurrency-to-GPU mapping in a notebook and produce a table, but high level: plan for 6-8 A100-80GB equiv for steady, with autoscale to 12-14 nodes on burst. If they want tighter p95 SLAs (<400ms) we should recommend more GPU headroom or H100s.

Also: they should scope KV cache retention for chat sessions (we’ll need estimated session lengths and prefix reuse rate). Paul, can you share typical session turn counts?

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

---

From: Paul Moreno <paul@crowdworks.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-05T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — CrowdWorks API migration

Marissa/Vivek — thanks, this is helpful. Answers inline: 

- The 48h sample is representative of normal weekday traffic (no campaigns).
- Session turns: typical chat session 4–7 turns (median 5), but heavy-users occasionally hit 12+ turns. Session reuse of context is high (~85%).
- Canary: we were thinking 10% initially, then 50% after a week if KPIs look good.
- Classification SLA: less strict — p95 acceptable up to 1.2s for the short classification calls.

Couple of asks for the sizing worksheet you mentioned: could you provide estimated tail latency at the different GPU counts, plus a cost delta estimate (monthly) between steady-only and steady+burst configurations? Also, we will need a short Mutual Action Plan for procurement events (deliverables, timelines, security review window).

Thanks — attaching an updated CSV with session-turn annotations.

Paul
--- attachment: cw_workload_samples_v2.csv (CSV, 18KB)

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Paul Moreno <paul@crowdworks.ai>, procurement@crowdworks.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-10T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — proposed estimate and next steps

Paul — quick summary and next steps (see attached redwood_sizing_estimate_v1.pdf and the Mutual Action Plan draft). Key points: 

1) Sizing summary (first-pass):
- Steady baseline: 8x A100-80GB-equivalent nodes to cover sustained 120 rps with median chat tokens (prompt+gen ~378 tokens) while meeting p95 ~550–600ms.
- Burst scale: autoscale policy to add up to 6 additional nodes during short bursts (targeting handling up to ~220 rps observed in the sample).
- Canary plan: route 10% traffic for 72 hours, monitor p95 latency, generation error rate, and token cost per request. If KPIs stable, promote to 50% for 7 days, then full cutover.

2) Performance tradeoffs:
- If CrowdWorks opts for H100-class instances (or equivalent) we project p95 improvement ~30–40% for the same node counts, which would allow a smaller steady pool (6 H100-equivalents).
- Increase in prefix cache retention (to leverage the 85% session reuse) can reduce per-request token compute by ~8–12% depending on average prompt overlap. We’ll work with engineering on cache key design during POC.

3) Cost and procurement: baseline monthly estimate (steady-only pool) vs steady+burst (attached PDF shows monthly cost deltas and a 12-month committed option with discounts).

4) Deliverables & timeline:
- Shared M.A.P. attached (mutual_action_plan.docx) with milestones: security questionnaire (SOC2 evidence), pilot deployment (2 weeks), canary (1 week), cutover window (1 week).
- Suggested security/ops handoff: schedule SOC2 evidence exchange within 5 business days of SOW signature.

Next steps: please review the PDF and MAP draft and let us know good times for a technical kick-off. We’ll also send a short sizing worksheet that shows per-node tail latency curves for your dataset (Ben is finishing the notebook).

Best,
Vivek
Director, Pre-Sales
Redwood Inference
